This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The test `testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM` calls `doTest("b:foo/test", DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM, "/b:foo[1]/test[1]")`. The `doTest` method creates a new `JXPathContext` with a `DocumentContainer` for the XML resource "InnerEmptyNamespace.xml" loaded as DOM model. Then it asserts that the pointer obtained by calling `context.getPointer("b:foo/test")` has the expected path `"/b:foo[1]/test[1]"`.

The bug report states that resetting the default XML namespace causes an infinite loop when calling `.asPath()` on a node with an empty namespace (e.g., `<test xmlns="">`). This is related to namespace handling in XPath when the default namespace changes inside XML elements.

The test involves the sample XML structure where an element `<test>` has an explicitly empty namespace (`xmlns=""`) inside an element with a default namespace set (`xmlns="test111"`). The path lookup `b:foo/test` tries to find the node `<test>` under `<b:foo>`, which triggers namespace processing in the pointer creation.

From the code snippets, `getPointer(xpath)` first compiles the XPath expression and then returns a `Pointer`. When the pointer's `asPath()` is called, it resolves the node's position and namespace context.

The reported infinite loop likely happens in the namespace context handling code when the default namespace switches from a URI to empty string inside the tree. The pointer's `asPath()` method, when constructing the XPath string for a node with a reset default namespace, may recursively query parent contexts or namespaces, never resolving due to the reset default namespace.

Thus the underlying bug is that when the XML namespace is reset to empty string (`xmlns=""`), the `.asPath()` method enters an endless loop in namespace resolution, failing to terminate and construct the correct XPath path.

This diagnosis fits the failure in `testInnerEmptyNamespaceDOM` because that test exercises precisely this XML node structure and calls `.asPath()` on a pointer obtained via the XPath `"b:foo/test"`. The infinite loop in `.asPath()` is the root cause of the test failure.

Next, it will be useful to inspect the implementation of the `Pointer.asPath()` method and namespace resolution methods it calls to confirm exactly where the loop happens.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
